Benchmark contamination and test-set leakage are significant concerns in the field of Large Language Models (LLMs), as they can lead to inflated performance metrics and misleading evaluations.

One highly relevant paper is **"TRUCE: Private Benchmarking to Prevent Contamination and Improve Comparative Evaluation of LLMs"** (arXiv:2403.00393). This paper directly addresses the issue, noting that because benchmarking is the standard for LLM evaluation, the fact that most open-source benchmarks have been contaminated or leaked into the training data of LLMs poses a major problem for the validity of these evaluations.

While the search results above highlight this specific work, researchers frequently discuss this issue in the broader context of model evaluation and data transparency. If you are researching this topic, I recommend focusing on papers that propose "private" or "dynamic" benchmarking, as they are specifically designed to circumvent the static nature of public benchmarks that are prone to leakage.
